subject: Lynx Health PoC — SLO envelopes, burst plan, and topology notes
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Vega <samantha.vega@lynxhealth.com>, procurement@lynxhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lynx Health discovery — immediate recap and PoC scope proposal

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same deck for procurement and engineering. I kept this focused on the latency/throughput constraints you emphasized and the burst capacity ask.

Short summary of pain / goals
- Primary pain: high variance in latency from your inference layer during peak user sessions (appointment search / triage workflows).
- Business goal: maintain p95 generation latency <= 350ms for conversational LLM calls under typical load; p50 target 120–150ms.
- Cost constraint: must fit within the pilot budget (~$8k/mo for hosted inference) while proving consistent tail latency during 2x weekly usage spikes.

Technical constraints you called out
- Typical prompt sizes: 220–400 tokens (system + context + user).
- Average concurrent QPS during peak: 12 sustained, with hourly bursts up to 70 QPS for ~3–8 minutes.
- Model family preference: open-model compatibility; willing to test a 30B–70B quantized variant if quality passes your eval set.
- KV cache usage: session affinity (relevant for triage flows) critical to hit lower tails.

Proposed PoC topology (short)
- Hosted Redwood API with a dedicated small pool for the PoC (reserved burst buckets).
- Two model variants: fast-quantized 30B for latency-sensitive paths, full-fp32/float16 70B for highest-quality fallbacks.
- Smart routing policy: route to low-latency pool first; fallback to higher-capacity pool when tokens per second exceed threshold, with automated throttling to preserve p95 SLO.
- KV prefix caching + 100ms batching window to optimize throughput without blowing the latency SLO.

Mutual action items (my notes)
1) Redwood: share a 1-page topology sketch and a draft PoC SOW (attached).
2) Lynx: confirm the peak-burst windows and provide a short sample of anonymized request traces (tokens per request and concurrency histogram).
3) Procurement: confirm timeline for PO; target PO by 2028-03-23 to start provisioning.
4) Engineering deep-dive: schedule a 60-min infra call week of 2028-03-13 to align autoscale knobs and canary plan.

Attachments: attached draft PoC scope (lynx_poc_scope_v0.3.pdf) and a quick topology sketch (redwood-topology-sketch.png).

I'll wait to hear back on the traces and procurement cadence. If we can lock the PO window this week, we can pre-stage a dedicated pool and run a short warmup test during your lower traffic hours.

Best,
Logan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Vega <samantha.vega@lynxhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Lynx Health discovery — immediate recap and PoC scope proposal

Logan — thanks, this is great and exactly the level we need for procurement. Quick confirmations and clarifications: 

1) Bursts: the 70 QPS spikes come from our marketing-driven check-ins and last ~4–7 minutes. They usually happen within a 30-minute window twice a day (PST).
2) Our priority is p95 for the triage path (those are the high-traffic sessions) but we also want to ensure the non-triage conversational flows stay below p99 2s.
3) We will sanitize and push a small sample of traces (CSV w/ token counts + timestamps) by Monday EOD.
4) Procurement: PO approver is on leave until 2028-03-16. We can do a conditional approval email before PO if we get a SOW and cost spreadsheet.

Next best dates for the engineering deep-dive: Mon 2028-03-13 afternoon (2–4pm PT) or Tue 2028-03-14 morning (9–11am PT). Either works for our infra lead.

Samantha
Director of Product — Lynx Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Vega <samantha.vega@lynxhealth.com>, procurement@lynxhealth.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lynx Health discovery — immediate recap and PoC scope proposal

Looping in a few technical specifics so engineering has something actionable for the deep-dive. High-level notes we should present to Lynx: 

- SLO breakdown to propose during the call:
  * PoC SLOs (target): p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 350ms (triage path); p99 <= 2s for non-triage.
  * Load guard: soft limit at 60 QPS sustained per pool, burst tokens handled via pre-warmed capacity with 45s warmup buckets.

- Batching & KV cache:
  * Use 75ms batching window for the triage flow if the QPS distribution suggests batching benefit; otherwise 30–50ms. We should plan to show a latency vs. batching tradeoff using their sample traces.
  * Prefix/KV cache: enable session-keyed cache with TTL 12h for triage sessions; this reduces redundant context token decoding.

- Model config & quantization:
  * Start with an FP16 34B variant (smaller memory footprint than 70B, better latency) using int8 quantization option in Redwood's runtime for the fast path. Reserve an FP16 70B as fallback (quality checks).
  * We'll run their eval set to check quality delta; if loss < 2% on their BLEU/ROUGE-style metric, we recommend the quantized 34B for scale.

- Topology sketch to show (attached PNG):
  * Front door: regional routing (us-west) -> low-latency dedicated pool (quantized model) -> fallback pool (full model).
  * Observability: per-route p50/p95/p99 panels, token-level cost, and per-session KV-hit rate.

Action items for the deep-dive:
- Logan: bring the cost spreadsheet and SOW version.
- Karthik: prepare a short demo of the KV cache behavior and a synthetic stress script that simulates their burst profile.
- Samantha: send traces and a 10–15 sample of the busiest session contexts (anonymized).

I will prepare two visual slides: one showing latency vs batching window, and another showing burst-handling behavior for the proposed pre-warmed bucket.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@lynxhealth.com
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lynx Health discovery — immediate recap and PoC scope proposal

Thanks all — attaching the same SOW and adding a short cost spreadsheet inline (see attachment). A couple of small clarifications ahead of Monday's deep-dive: 

- Cost note: the PoC pricing in the sheet assumes 24/7 hosted pool with a 2x pre-warm factor for two 10-minute daily marketing bursts. If Lynx prefers to only pay for on-demand burst minutes we can show an alternate bucket billing model; procurement: we should align which model you need for the PO.

- Canary plan sketch:
  * Step 0: pre-warm a 3-node quantized pool and run a 60-minute warmup with synthetic traces (off-peak) to populate KV cache.
  * Step 1: small percentage (5%) traffic shift for 30 minutes; monitor p95 and KV-hit.
  * Step 2: ramp to 20% and then 100% if p95 stays within SLO. Automatic fallback to full model if error rate or p99 > 2s.

- Engineering deep-dive confirmed: Mon 2028-03-13 14:30–15:30 PT (locked). I'll send a calendar invite.

Next actions (for the thread):
- Samantha: traces + procurement's guidance on billing model by 2028-03-12.
- Karthik: share the synthetic burst script and a short readme before the deep-dive.
- Marissa: slide deck + topology PNG (attached).

[Attachment: lynx_poc_scope_v0.3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: redwood-topology-sketch.png (PNG)]

Looking forward — we'll aim to have a working pilot within 10 business days of PO.

Cheers,
Logan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
